# Ninth review of SEEN-108, attempt 12, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned fresh on opus with the task text of triage record 127, and asked to
judge two things rather than take them on trust: whether record 121's fix closes
the eighth review's blocker without opening something else, and whether
criterion 3 as twice amended is still a criterion worth having. Verdict
`return`, five findings, one high.

It confirmed the blocker closed at the root rather than patched:
`implementer_default` reads thresholds.toml and nothing else, `routed`,
`ticket_in_hand`, `_records` and `_delivered` are gone with no dangling
references, the three `agents.sync` calls are gone, and `FixedCopiesTest`
asserts the four states that were wrong all leave the copies identical and
doctor clean. It verified 843 tests green and doctor clean at HEAD itself. On
criterion 3 it judged the criterion worth having and the gate behind it the most
carefully built thing in the diff, and located the 0.66 score's real cause in
F1 rather than in the criterion.

- **F1, high.** The fix removed the routed model and effort from the Codex agent
  TOML as well as the Claude Code copy, so nothing carries a route to a Codex
  implementer, while `routing.implementer_task`, `agents.implementer_default`'s
  docstring and the second amendment to criterion 3 all still say the TOML does.
  A Codex session reads the spawn text, opens the file, finds opus at high
  effort, works the slice on opus, and records its checks declaring the routed
  haiku, so the gate compares haiku with haiku and advances; kpi.json then
  reports a routed cost nothing on haiku earned, which is the figure SEEN-109
  calibrates on. The cost record 121 was offered named only the Claude Code
  effort; as built it is both keys on both assistants.
- **F2, medium.** The skill both assistants read contradicts itself: line 64
  says the copies do not vary by slice, line 110 says sync rewrites them at
  every slice boundary, and the comments in thresholds.toml and agents.py repeat
  the abandoned claim. A session that believes line 110 edits the file by hand,
  which doctor then reports as drift.
- **F3, medium.** The routing rules match a slice's declared file list rather
  than the files it changes. A plan that does not foresee `packages/core` sends
  money arithmetic into the Jev request like any other slice, and with shadow
  off it can be written by the weakest tier, which is the one case the rules
  exist to prevent. `slice_files` reports the divergence at the review triage,
  after the code is written, and nothing re-routes or refuses. On this ticket it
  has failed all eight triages, by 22 files.
- **F4, low.** Record 9 is the only route record in the repository, written at
  attempt 1, and carries no `implementer_task` and no `model_passed`, so
  criterion 3's "from the spawn instruction the route record carries" has no
  instance on the branch that delivers it. Nothing crashes, because no reader
  indexes those keys, which is why eight reviews and four deterministic checks
  did not see it.
- **F5, low.** The tests that were about the per-slice design still document it
  as current: `ImplementerCopyTest`'s docstring says the copies are generated
  per slice because Claude Code documents no per-invocation effort override, and
  it keeps three helpers no remaining test calls, one of them written precisely
  to catch a boundary that failed to rewrite the file.
